plugins.description: Unofficial visual control panel and MCP bridge for DeepSeek Harness: model, workspace and permission controls, task monitoring, and reusable sessions.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-mcp-bridge

English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

**A visible control panel for Claude Code and Codex delegation to DeepSeek Harness.** Choose the model, provider, workspace, and new-session permissions in Harness; inspect task state through MCP; find and continue the resulting conversations.

This project is for people who want to spend less of their main model's effort on bounded supporting tasks, and make repeated Harness calls and the resulting sessions easier to manage.

> Third-party, unofficial integration. Not affiliated with or endorsed by DeepSeek, Anthropic, or OpenAI. Harness interfaces and MCP clients can change; check the compatibility notes before upgrading.

> **Archive-only maintenance in 0.2.4:** permanent deletion is disabled in every plugin entry point. The compatible `autoCleanupDays` setting now archives eligible MCP-created sessions, keeps their files, and uses the official non-stopping option; `0` turns automatic archival off. Old pending-delete files are retained unchanged and never executed. See [maintenance boundaries and upgrade notes](docs/troubleshooting.md#cleanup-limitation-and-pending-deletions).

## Why this bridge?

- **Delegate selectively.** Send a narrow review, summary, documentation task, or investigation to Harness, then bring the result back to your main agent.
- **Keep responsibility clear.** The main agent still scopes the task, checks the result, and integrates useful work.
- **Keep controls visible.** Use Harness's toolbar for task constraints and its conversations for context; use MCP status/results to inspect execution rather than relying on a silent handoff.
- **Manage repeated delegation.** Find task IDs after a disconnect, continue managed sessions, and archive conversations you want to keep.

Delegation can reduce the amount of work the main model performs, but it does not guarantee a fixed quota reduction, lower total cost, or faster completion. DeepSeek or your chosen provider can still charge for delegated work, and coordination, retries, and review still consume resources. See [choosing and measuring delegated tasks](docs/delegation.md).

## How it fits together

1. Claude Code, Codex, or another compatible MCP client sends a tool request.
2. The local bridge connects that request to the plugin running in DeepSeek Harness.
3. A Harness agent uses the configured provider, workspace, and execution permissions.
4. The client receives the task result for review and further work.

**A local bridge does not mean local model inference.** Prompts and relevant workspace content may be sent to the provider configured in Harness. Check your provider's terms and your own data-sharing permissions before delegating private material.

The current plugin installs into the **desktop profile**, so that Harness host must be running. This is a good fit if you already use Harness and delegate frequently. A one-off task may not justify the extra installation and process. Harness also has an official CLI; other hosting profiles for this plugin have not been verified. [CLI and hosting FAQ](docs/troubleshooting.md#does-harness-have-a-cli).

## Quick start

Bridge version: **0.2.4**. Target Harness desktop version: **0.2.1-rc.2**. Build with Node.js **22+** and npm. Maintainer-provided verification notes cover Windows; they do not establish support for every platform or MCP client.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/FishCityBee/dsh-mcp-bridge.git
cd dsh-mcp-bridge
npm ci
npm run build
```

Install `dist-package/` with Harness's bundled CLI. Windows PowerShell example, with paths replaced for your installation:

```powershell
& "D:\Program Files\Deepseek Harness\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd" plugin --profile desktop add "C:\path\to\dsh-mcp-bridge\dist-package"
```

Completely quit Harness, including the tray process, and reopen it. In the bridge toolbar, select your provider/model, a disposable default workspace, and read-only new-session permissions. Automatic archival defaults to off; enable it only after reviewing its scope.

Register the relay in the client you use, with its absolute path:

```sh
# Claude Code
claude mcp add --transport stdio --scope user dsh-harness -- node "C:/path/to/dsh-mcp-bridge/dist-package/bin/stdio.mjs"

# Codex
codex mcp add dsh-harness -- node "C:/path/to/dsh-mcp-bridge/dist-package/bin/stdio.mjs"
```

Ask the client to call `harness_status`, `list_models`, and `list_workspaces` before starting a task. Then try one small task with no file changes. Model tasks can incur provider charges. See [installation, timeouts, environment variables, and upgrade steps](docs/installation.md) for complete instructions and official client references.

## Controls that matter

- **Model constraints:** single-model mode locks provider/model/effort. Provider mode also locks model/effort unless the user enables caller overrides; the provider stays locked.
- **Execution evidence:** requested and effective model selections are separate. `effectiveSelection` is populated only after the bridge observes a request, and does not prove provider acceptance or billing.
- **Permissions:** new-session presets use Harness's official permission service; that selector leaves existing sessions unchanged. Full access is a high-risk option, not a setup requirement.
- **Task lifecycle:** start, wait, inspect, find, and cancel tasks. Client disconnects are separate from task cancellation; cancellation cannot undo completed effects.
- **Sessions:** continue bridge-managed conversations and archive/unarchive them. Automatic maintenance only archives; permanent deletion is unavailable.

The default connection uses a local pipe/socket with the stdio relay, without opening a TCP port. Optional HTTP is off by default. Update the plugin and the entire relay together; 0.2.4 uses `tls-pinned-v3` and does not fall back to older handshakes.

## Documentation

- [Installation and Claude Code / Codex setup](docs/installation.md)
- [Configuration, model defaults, and permission boundaries](docs/configuration.md)
- [Tool reference, task recovery, and session maintenance](docs/usage.md)
- [Troubleshooting and FAQ](docs/troubleshooting.md)
- [Delegating useful work](docs/delegation.md)
- [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [Security and responsible reporting](SECURITY.md)

## Permission boundaries

There are two separate decisions: whether your MCP client may call a bridge tool, and whether the Harness agent may perform an operation. Client-side MCP approval is not a replacement for Harness execution approval. Choosing a workspace does not by itself sandbox an agent.

Start in a disposable workspace with a small, read-only task. Keep credentials out of prompts, screenshots, and issue reports. Review substantive results before accepting changes. Back up important session data. Plugin deletion stays disabled until an official safe cross-process deletion boundary is available.

## Compatibility and verification

This bridge relies on version-specific Harness APIs and storage behavior. Other Harness versions, alternate profiles, and all client/platform combinations are not implied to be supported.

The repository includes maintainer-written technical records in Chinese: [reliability changes](docs/audit-2026-10-17.md), [desktop transport checks](docs/desktop-2026-10-18.md), and [new-session permission checks](docs/ui-permissions-2026-10-18.md). The [0.2.4 maintenance notes](docs/recheck-0.2.4.md) distinguish the current changes from earlier historical reports. Their stated test scope and remaining gaps matter; they are not a claim that all security risks or UI paths have been validated.

## Contribute

Bug reports, compatibility checks, translations, and focused pull requests are welcome in English or Chinese. Please read the [contribution guide](CONTRIBUTING.md), and keep secrets and private session content out of public reports.

If this project helps your workflow, a star helps others discover it.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE). The existing copyright and license notices apply.

# dsh-rea-toggle

[English](#english) · [中文](#中文)

One switch per conversation that decides whether the **REA**
(`reverse-engineer-anything`) MCP server's context reaches the model at all.

REA registers **207 tool schemas** plus a multi-kilobyte server-instructions
block. `dsh-mcp-client` puts both on the **global** layer, so every agent pays
for them on every request — whether or not the turn has anything to do with
reverse engineering.

With this plugin installed, a small pill appears below the composer:

- **REA on** (green) — exactly the pre-install behaviour. REA's tools and
  instructions are visible to the model.
- **REA off** (grey) — those 207 tool schemas and the `mcp:rea` instructions
  block **leave the model context**, taking effect on the next step.

**The switch is per conversation.** Each conversation remembers its own
position, and a new conversation starts **off**. That is the whole point: a
conversation about a web app should not pay for 207 reverse-engineering schemas
just because some other conversation needs them. Subagents inherit the position
of the conversation that created them, so delegating inside reverse-engineering
work does not silently break the subagent.

The same switch is on the keyboard: `/rea off`, `/rea on`, `/rea status`,
`/rea toggle` — all acting on the conversation you typed them in.

Nothing is uninstalled and nothing restarts. The MCP connection stays up; the
model simply stops being told those tools exist.

---

## English

### What it actually does

The token cost comes from two different places that travel two different paths,
so one mechanism is not enough:

| Target | Mechanism |
| --- | --- |
| Tool schemas | `tools.restrict({ deny })` is called **in each agent's own context**. `ToolRuntime.view()` filters what that scope *inherits* from the global layer, and the model-facing schema list is rebuilt from that view on every assembly. The reserved `run_code` transport sits outside the filterable layers, so it is unaffected. |
| Instructions text | `dsh-mcp-client` registers the server instructions as a prompt section named `mcp:<server>` at order `MCP_SERVERS` (3100). **A scoped section with the same name shadows the global one** — a documented contract of `systemPrompt.section()` ("a scoped section shadows a global section with the same name"), not an implementation detail — and an empty section is dropped at render (`renderPrompt` keeps only `text.length > 0`). Registering that name and returning `''` therefore removes the block for that agent alone. |

Both are scoped registrations, so disposing them restores the previous state
exactly. That is why flipping the switch needs no restart and no reload.

Coverage includes **subagents**: `agent/created` is serial and awaited by the
registry, so installing inside it lands ahead of any prompt assembly.

### Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:aurumple/dsh-rea-toggle
```

Or point at a checkout:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-rea-toggle
```

The bundle row id is `rea-toggle`; the package name is `dsh-rea-toggle`.

### Use

| Where | What |
| --- | --- |
| Pill under the composer | Click to flip **this conversation**. Green = on, grey = off, red border = the host did not answer. |
| `/rea off` · `/rea on` | Set this conversation's position. `enable` / `disable` work too. |
| `/rea toggle` | Flip this conversation. |
| `/rea status` | Report this conversation's position. |

A new conversation starts off. The first time you turn one on, that conversation
is remembered; conversations you never touch stay on the default and are not
written down.

Positions are remembered in `$DSH_HOME/rea-toggle.json` (usually
`~/.dsh/rea-toggle.json`), keyed by session id, and survive a restart. The file
keeps the 500 most recently changed conversations; an older one simply falls
back to the default.

### Configuration

Every field is optional.

```yaml
- id: rea-toggle
  name: dsh-rea-toggle
  config:
    server: rea               # one MCP server to govern; default "rea"
    # servers: [rea, ghidra]  # or several; wins over `server` when present
    # defaultEnabled: true    # new conversations start ON instead of off
```

Changing `server` governs a different MCP server by the same rules: tool prefix
`mcp__<server>__`, instructions section `mcp:<server>`. Because the mechanism is
generic, this works for any MCP server whose tools are bridged by
`dsh-mcp-client` — the REA case is just the one that motivated it.

`defaultEnabled` exists for anyone who wants the pre-plugin behaviour back: with
it on, a conversation nobody has switched behaves exactly as if this plugin were
not installed.

### HTTP API

The Client half talks to the Host over one exact route on the bare `webServer`
(the same shape other bundles use, so it does not travel through the `/api`
prefix fence). The conversation is `session=` on GET and a body field on POST:
the pill always knows which conversation it is showing, and a request that does
not say cannot be answered for it.

```
GET  /rea-toggle/state?session=<id>
  -> { session, enabled, known, defaultEnabled, servers, agents, tools, statePath }

GET  /rea-toggle/state            (no session: a summary)
  -> { session: null, defaultEnabled, servers, conversations, agents, tools, statePath }

POST /rea-toggle/state
  body: { "session": "<id>", "enabled": true | false }   (omit `enabled` to flip)
  -> the per-conversation status object
```

`known` says whether this conversation has ever been switched; when it is
`false`, `enabled` is just `defaultEnabled` and nothing has been written yet.
`agents` is how many live agents of that conversation are currently covered;
`tools` is how many of the governed server's tools were recognised, which is the
honest answer to "did it find REA at all" — if it reads `0`, the server is not
connected under that name (and stays `0`-safe because `restrictableNames` is the
denyable set, not the filtered view).

### Scope and limits

- **One server per row by default.** Other MCP servers are untouched; use
  `servers` to govern more than one.
- **Hidden, not unloaded.** The MCP connection stays up and the REA process
  keeps running. When the switch is off the model simply cannot reach it —
  including indirectly through `run_code`. That is deliberate: leaving a second
  path open would save only half the tokens.
- **Per-conversation state, in-process.** Positions are read from the file at
  `apply()` and written on every change. Two DSH instances sharing one profile
  each read it once and do not live-sync with each other.
- **It does not delete anything.** Turning it off is reversible in one click,
  and uninstalling the bundle lifts every registration.

### Verify it yourself

The claim is that the tools are gone from the model's context, not merely
hidden in a UI. Check it where the model's own view is exposed:

1. With the switch **on**, ask the agent to list its tools — `mcp__rea__*`
   entries are there (207 of them for a stock REA install).
2. Turn it **off**, ask again — they are gone, and calling one by name returns
   `Error: unknown tool "mcp__rea__binary_session"`.
3. Turn it back **on** — they return, unchanged.
4. Open a **second conversation** and check its tool list: it is off, while the
   first one is still on. That is the property that distinguishes this plugin
   from a global toggle.

### Development

```bash
npm test        # node:test, no dependencies
```

The suite drives the real `apply()` against a small model of the three
contracts it depends on (tool view, prompt section merge, agent registry). It
pins what "off" removes, that "on" restores the previous state exactly, that a
new subagent is covered before its first step, that the position survives a
restart, and that the HTTP surface validates its input.

### License

MIT

服务器的上下文是否进入模型。

REA 注册了 **207 个工具 schema**，外加一段几千字的服务端说明。
`dsh-mcp-client` 把它们放在**全局层**，所以每个 agent、每次请求都在为它们付

plugins.description: Ordered web-search failover provider for DeepSeek Harness: try backends in priority order, fall back automatically.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-web-search-failover

DeepSeek Harness 的搜索故障转移插件：按顺序尝试多个搜索后端，前一个失败（HTTP 错误、没有 `web_search_tool_result` 结果块、或返回空结果）时自动落到下一个。

> **English.** A failover web-search provider for DeepSeek Harness. The harness resolves exactly one search provider per `ctx.web` seam and a provider carries a single `model`, so one upstream error kills the whole search. This bundle registers a `deepseek-failover` provider that walks an ordered list of backends — same request, next backend on any failure (throw, abort excepted, or an empty result) — and only fails when every backend did. The stock `web-search-deepseek` row is disabled by the bundle's own patch, so no manual profile editing is needed. Node ≥ 22, harness ≥ 0.2.1, MIT.

## 为什么需要它

Harness 的 `ctx.web` 每次只解析一个 search provider，provider 也只有单个 `model` 字段，没有失败重试链；`web-search-deepseek` 一旦上游出错，整次搜索就失败。new-api 的自动换渠道只在“同一个模型名有多个渠道”时生效，所以要么在网关造一个别名，要么在 harness 侧做转移。本插件选后者：网关保持官方模型名。

## 兼容性

| 平台 | 支持 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10/11（PowerShell 7 或 5.1） | ✅ | `dsh plugin` 本身跨平台；本文所有命令在 PowerShell 里原样可跑 |
| macOS（zsh / bash） | ✅ | 原生路径 |
| Linux | ✅ | 原生路径 |

前置条件：

- **DSH ≥ 0.2.1** — 插件复用 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-search-deepseek` 导出的 `DeepSeekSearchProvider`，0.2.0 没有这个接口
- **Node ≥ 22**，且 **`pnpm` 在 `PATH` 上**（`dsh plugin` 内部调 pnpm）
- 能访问 `https://codeload.github.com`（public 仓库，不需要 token）
- 一个 OpenAI/Anthropic 兼容的搜索网关，以及它的 API key

## 安装

一条命令（自动写依赖、写 `dsh.profile.bundles`、并跑 `pnpm install`）：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:xingzoudefengye/dsh-web-search-failover
```

```powershell
# Windows 上完全一样
dsh plugin --profile web add github:xingzoudefengye/dsh-web-search-failover
```

然后**重启 DSH**（关掉 `dsh web` 的终端再重新起）。插件是在 host 启动时 import 的，不重启不会生效 —— 详见排错第 1 条。

Desktop 版 profile 名是 `desktop`，需要先**完全退出应用**再加：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:xingzoudefengye/dsh-web-search-failover
```

插件没有 `prepare` 脚本、没有构建步骤，纯 JS，不会触发 pnpm 的 `allowBuilds` 拦截。

### 凭据

插件的 `apiKeyEnv` 指向一个**凭据引用名**，不是明文。把网关令牌写进 harness 的凭据文件：

- macOS / Linux：`~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml`
- Windows：`%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\.credentials.yaml`

```yaml
refs:
  NEWAPI_API_KEY: sk-...
```

这个文件由 harness 的 credentials 插件注入，**不需要写系统环境变量**。如果你更习惯环境变量，把 `apiKeyEnv` 改成对应的变量名即可。

### 不想用 CLI 时

手工改 profile 的 `package.json` 效果一样：

```jsonc
"dependencies": {
  "dsh-web-search-failover": "github:xingzoudefengye/dsh-web-search-failover"
},
"dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": [ "...", "dsh-web-search-failover" ] } }
```

再在 profile 目录（如 `~/.dsh/profiles/web`，Windows 是 `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\web`）跑 `pnpm install`，重启 DSH。

## 验证

```bash
dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep -A3 "searchProvider"
```

```powershell
dsh --profile web --dump-config | Select-String -Pattern "searchProvider" -Context 0,3
```

应看到 `searchProvider: deepseek-failover`。再做一次真实搜索，网关日志里会出现主后端的模型名；只有主后端失败时才会多一条备用后端。

**关于默认网关地址**：插件自带的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里 `baseURL` 写的是一个示例网关（`http://43.133.21.227:3000/v1`）。用别人的地址跑不通，**请改成你自己的网关**，见下一节。

## 配置

在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里覆盖 `id: web-search-failover` 这一行的 `config`：

```yaml
- id: web-search-failover
  config:
    providerId: deepseek-failover   # ctx.web 选中的 provider 名，一般不用改
    backends:
      - { model: claude-haiku-5-5,   baseURL: https://your-gateway/v1, apiKeyEnv: NEWAPI_API_KEY }
      - { model: deepseek-v4-flash,  baseURL: https://your-gateway/v1, apiKeyEnv: NEWAPI_API_KEY }
```

| 键 | 默认 | 作用 |
|---|---|---|
| `providerId` | `deepseek-failover` | 注册给 `ctx.web` 的 provider 名；bundle patch 里 `web.searchProvider` 必须与它一致 |
| `backends` | — | **有序**列表，第 0 个优先，其后都是备胎；每项 `model` / `baseURL` / `apiKeyEnv` 各自独立 |
| `apiKeyEnv` / `baseURL` / `apiKey` / `apiVersion` / `maxTokens` / `maxUses` | 见 `lib/index.js` 的 `Config` | 旧式单后端字段；用 `backends` 时不需要，插件按 backend 逐个构造 provider |

失败判定：抛错、或者成功但没有 sources。`WEB_ABORTED`（用户取消）直接向上抛，不换后端 —— 取消不该触发备用后端。全部失败才返回最后一个错误；如果所有后端都成功但确实没结果，返回那个空结果。

## 卸载

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-web-search-failover
```

然后重启 DSH。bundle 的 patch 随之失效，harness 原有的 `web-search-deepseek` 行会恢复；如果你之前手工在 profile patch 里删过它，需要自己加回来。

## 排错

| 现象 | 原因 | 处理 |
|---|---|---|
| `dsh plugin add` 成功，但搜索行为没变 | 插件在 host 进程启动时 import，进程里的模块不会热替换 | 重启 DSH（关掉 `dsh web` 再起） |
| 改了插件源码（哪怕是 `lib/index.js`）也不生效 | Node 的 ESM 缓存：已 import 的模块不会重新执行 | 同上，重启 host；GitHub 安装还需先 `dsh plugin add` 重装以拉新代码 |
| `dsh plugin add` 卡住或报网络错误 | 拉的是 `codeload.github.com` 的 tarball，公司网络/代理常拦 | 走代理，或把仓库整目录拷过去，依赖改成 `file:` 路径后 `pnpm install`（插件无外部 npm 依赖，离线可装） |
| 报 `WEB_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` | 所有 backends 都 `available() === false`，通常是 `apiKeyEnv` 指向的引用没有值 | 检查 `.credentials.yaml` 的 `refs:` 里有该键，且键名与 `apiKeyEnv` 完全一致 |
| 搜索一直是备用后端的模型 | 主后端失败但未报错（返回空结果也会触发回落） | 看网关日志确认主后端返回码；密钥额度、模型名拼写是最常见原因 |
| 配置树里出现同一个 row id 冲突（`web-search-deepseek` 被两处同时声明） | profile patch 里手工加过 `id: web-search-deepseek` 的行，与 bundle patch 打架 | 删掉 profile 里那一行，插件自带的 patch 已负责禁用它 |

## 同步到另一台机器

逻辑全在插件里，换机器不需要搬配置，但要满足四件事：

1. **装插件**：跑上面那条 `dsh plugin add`。版本自动跟 `master` 最新提交，两台机器不必同 commit，但 harness 版本要一致（都 ≥ 0.2.1）。
2. **凭据**：`.credentials.yaml` 的 `refs:` 里要有 `NEWAPI_API_KEY`。
3. **清掉旧的 provider 行**：profile patch 里若还有 `- id: web-search-deepseek`，删掉。
4. **网关可达**：`baseURL` 换成本机可访问的地址。

## 开发

本仓库是纯 JS、无构建步骤。仓库里没有 `node_modules`，直接 `npm test` 会因为找不到 `@deepseek-ai/*` 的 peer 依赖而失败 —— 先把本机已安装的 harness 包链进来：

```bash
node scripts/dev-link.mjs            # 探测 dsh 的安装位置，链入 schemastery / dsh-web / dsh-web-search-deepseek 等
npm test                             # node --test
```

`dev-link` 依次探测：`dsh` 可执行文件所在的 npm 目录、`$DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>`、`$DSH_HOME/profiles`、`$DSH_HOME`，也可以用第一个参数或 `DSH_PACKAGE_DIR` 直接指定 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` 所在目录。Windows 上用 junction，不需要管理员权限。

改完代码在本地验证，再装到 profile：`dsh plugin --profile web add <本仓库绝对路径>` 走 `link:` 依赖，配合 `dev-link` 即可改完重启 host 就看到效果。

## 相关插件

同作者、同一套安装方式（`dsh plugin add github:xingzoudefengye/<repo>`）：

- [dsh-browser](https://github.com/xingzoudefengye/dsh-browser) — 给 agent 一个可驱动的真实浏览器，侧栏并排显示
- [dsh-compaction-local-handoff](https://github.com/xingzoudefengye/dsh-compaction-local-handoff) — 无模型的本地交接式压缩
- [dsh-project-memory](https://github.com/xingzoudefengye/dsh-project-memory) — 有界、可提交进 git 的项目记忆
- [dsh-resume-budget](https://github.com/xingzoudefengye/dsh-resume-budget) — 会话恢复时的输入预算控制
- [dsh-session-recall](https://github.com/xingzoudefengye/dsh-session-recall) — 无模型、有界的会话史书

## 许可

MIT © xingzoudefengye，见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)。

plugins.description: Codex-style Windows computer use for DeepSeek Harness: UI Automation + screenshots + SendInput, liquid-glass screen overlay, ESC kill switch. Install: dsh plugin --profile web add github:esch30636/dsh-computer-use
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-computer-use

[![GitHub release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/esch30636/dsh-computer-use?sort=semver)](https://github.com/esch30636/dsh-computer-use/releases)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![dsh-plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/topic-dsh--plugin-4B5563)](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin)

Codex-style **Windows computer use** for DeepSeek Harness: window-targeted UI Automation + occlusion-tolerant screenshots + SendInput mouse/keyboard injection, exposed as five model-facing tools and backed by a bundled long-lived PowerShell helper.

While computer use is active, a click-through **screen overlay** draws a vivid "liquid glass" look: a sapphire *edge vignette* (fully clear center, satin-navy darkening toward the four screen edges) with a thin cyan glass rim hugging the display border, plus a "dynamic island" status pill at the top center — sapphire gradient, diagonal sheen, bright rim, breathing blue glow: `DeepSeek Harness 正在操控你的电脑 | 按 ESC 终止`. Pressing **ESC** stops computer use immediately and closes the overlay; the agent is told to stop and reports back.

Designed after the OpenAI Codex Windows Computer Use surface (`list_apps` / `get_window_state` / `click(element_index | x,y)` / `press_key` / `type_text` / `scroll` / `drag` / `set_value` / `activate_window`, X11-keysym-style key names, one action then re-observe), reimplemented as a pure DSH plugin with no third-party runtime dependencies.

## What you get

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `computer_list_windows` | List targetable top-level windows (window_id, process identity, title, rect, foreground/minimized, policy-blocked flag). Optionally lists Start-menu launchable apps. |
| `computer_observe` | Capture one window state: screenshot (default) and/or UI Automation tree with element indexes, focused element, selection, document text. Returns `state_id` + screenshot coordinate mapping. |
| `computer_action` | Exactly one action against a state: click / double_click / right_click / middle_click / mouse_move / type / key / scroll / drag / set_value / wait / activate_window. |
| `computer_launch_app` | Launch by exe path, exe name, Start-menu display name, `.lnk`, or `shell:AppsFolder\<AUMID>`; reports the windows it opened. |
| `computer_sequence` | Run up to 100 ordered input steps on one window without re-observing between them (absolute screen pixels) — for repetitive GUI work such as drawing a diagram; optionally returns one verification screenshot. |

Plus the click-through status overlay with the **ESC kill switch** (`USER_ESCAPE`), a system-prompt section (workflow, hard denies, confirmation policy) and a `computer-use` skill with the full playbook.

## Requirements

- Windows 10/11, interactive user session (not a service session), PowerShell 5.1 (`powershell.exe` — pwsh 7 not required).
- DSH 0.2.x (web/desktop profile; any composition that mounts `tools`, `systemPrompt` and `attachments` — the shipped base mounts all three).
- No native modules, no npm dependencies, no MCP server.

## Install

### Option A — DSH CLI (`dsh plugin add`)

For profiles the `dsh` CLI can manage (`web`, `tui`, `headless`, …), the plugin
installs as a regular DSH bundle:

```sh
# straight from GitHub (pnpm fetches the repo tarball)
dsh plugin --profile web add github:esch30636/dsh-computer-use

# or from the release tarball (no git fetch; works behind a GitHub proxy too)
dsh plugin --profile web add "https://github.com/esch30636/dsh-computer-use/releases/latest/download/dsh-computer-use.tgz"
```

`dsh plugin` installs the package into the profile and enables its bundle.
Restart the host (or let HMR recompose) and the `computer_*` tools appear in a
new session.

### Option B — Desktop app (`desktop` profile)

The Desktop app owns its reserved `desktop` profile, so `dsh plugin --profile
desktop` deliberately refuses to run there. Two supported paths:

1. **Plugin market** — after this plugin is listed in
   [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com) (submission pending the
   one-day repository age rule), open **设置 → 插件市场** and install it with one
   click.
2. **Release installer** (works immediately, no git/pnpm needed): download and
   unzip the archive from
   [releases](https://github.com/esch30636/dsh-computer-use/releases), then run
   inside the unzipped folder:

   ```powershell
   # downloads the latest release tarball and installs into the desktop profile
   powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\install-release.ps1
   ```

   Pin a version with `-Version v1.1.0`; target another profile with
   `-Profile web`; add `-Verify` to run the offline composition dump afterwards.

### Option C — manual / fully offline

Download the release archive
([releases](https://github.com/esch30636/dsh-computer-use/releases)), unzip it,
then run the bundled installer:

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\install.ps1 -Profile desktop
```

The installer copies the package to `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/node_modules/dsh-computer-use`, appends `dsh-computer-use` to `dsh.profile.bundles` (backing up `package.json`), and installs the skill to `%USERPROFILE%\.agents\skills\computer-use`. It works for any profile, e.g. `-Profile cu-test`, and `-Verify` dumps the composed profile offline.

Uninstall:

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\install.ps1 -Profile desktop -Uninstall
```

> **Note on the package name:** an unrelated npm package already uses the name
> `dsh-computer-use`, so `dsh plugin add dsh-computer-use` would install that one.
> Install this plugin through the GitHub spec or the release tarball URL shown
> above. Windows-only (`os: win32`): the helper drives a real interactive desktop
> session via UI Automation + SendInput.

## Configure

Options go in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (the row id is `computer-use`):

```yaml
- id: computer-use
  config:
    # extra process names/paths to deny (built-in denies always stay unless an
    # allow-* escape hatch is enabled)
    blockedProcesses: [msedge.exe]
    # allowlist mode: only these processes may be automated
    # allowedProcesses: [notepad.exe, mspaint.exe]
    screenshotMaxWidth: 1600
    screenshotMaxHeight: 1200
    maxElements: 600
    maxTreeDepth: 12
    idleTimeoutMs: 600000
    startupTimeoutMs: 90000
    requestTimeoutMs: 30000
    confirmRiskyActions: true
    warnWhenApprovalUnavailable: true
    allowWindowsKey: false
    allowTerminalAutomation: false
    keepScreenshots: false
    # screen overlay + ESC kill switch
    overlayEnabled: true
    overlayMessage: "DeepSeek Harness 正在操控你的电脑　|　按 ESC 终止"
    overlayIdleTimeoutMs: 90000
    overlayEdgeOpacity: 55
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `helperPath` | bundled | Override the helper script path. |
| `powershellPath` | `powershell.exe` | PowerShell used to host the helper. |
| `idleTimeoutMs` | `600000` | Kill the idle helper; it restarts on the next call. |
| `startupTimeoutMs` | `90000` | First-call budget (PowerShell start + Add-Type compile). |
| `requestTimeoutMs` | `30000` | Per-request budget once warm (screenshots/UIA use longer internal budgets). |
| `screenshotMaxWidth` / `screenshotMaxHeight` | `1600` / `1200` | Helper-side downscale bounds before the attachment store. |
| `maxElements` / `maxTreeDepth` / `maxTextChars` | `600` / `12` / `20000` | Accessibility tree bounds. |
| `blockedProcesses` / `blockedWindowClasses` | `[]` | Extra denials added to the built-in list. |
| `allowedProcesses` | `[]` | When non-empty: allowlist mode (everything else is denied). |
| `keepScreenshots` | `false` | Keep captured PNGs in `%TEMP%\dsh-computer-use` for debugging. |
| `confirmRiskyActions` | `true` | Ask through `ctx.approval` before destructive/externally visible actions. |
| `warnWhenApprovalUnavailable` | `true` | Under approval policy `never`/no channel: continue with a WARNING instead of failing. Set false for fail-closed. |
| `allowWindowsKey` / `allowTerminalAutomation` | `false` | Escape hatches for the two most dangerous hard denies (still discouraged; the helper keeps its own che

plugins.description: DSH 插件：在插件设置卡里调会话自动压缩的触发阈值与保留比例，保存即时写进 agent preset 隔离的压缩引擎
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-compaction-threshold

在 **插件 → dsh-compaction-threshold** 的配置卡里调 DSH 的会话压缩阈值，保存后即时生效，不需要重启。

| 设置项 | 默认 | 范围 | 说明 |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| 触发阈值 | 80% | 17–90 | 自动压缩在**已路由模型上下文窗口**的百分之多少处触发 |
| 保留近期对话 | 16% | 1–89 | 压缩时逐字保留的最近对话比例，必须小于触发阈值 |
| 自动压缩 | 开 | — | 关闭后不再自动压缩，手动 `/compact` 仍可用 |

例：窗口 1,000,000 的模型，触发阈值 80% → 800,000 tokens 处压缩，逐字保留 160,000 tokens。

## 为什么不能只改 profile 配置

DSH 内核**本来就带压缩**（`@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic`，默认 `thresholdRatio = 0.8` /
`retainRatio = 0.16`），但在 web / desktop 装配下**改不到**：

- 组合里**进程级**那一行 `compaction-basic` 是被禁用的；
- 每个 **agent preset 在自己的隔离 realm 里各挂一个** `BasicCompactionEngine`
  （`presets/cordis/agent.cordis.yml` 的 `compaction` 组，`isolate: { compaction: true }`）；
- 往 `~/.dsh/profiles/<name>/cordis.patch.yml` 写同 id 行**不落到会话实际用的那个引擎**。

## 实现要点（内核 0.1.5-rc.2 实测）

1. **取得引擎**：`ctx.get('agentPresets').serviceFor(agent, 'compaction')`
   → 返回该会话所在 preset 隔离 realm 内的 `BasicCompactionEngine`。
2. **改值的正确姿势是「替换整个 config 对象」，不能原位赋值**：
   - `Object.isFrozen(engine.config) === true`，而 `config` 属性本身 `writable: true`；
   - 原位赋值在 ESM 严格模式下抛 `TypeError: Cannot assign to read only property 'thresholdRatio'`，
     被 `try/catch` 吞掉就等于**静默什么都没做**（这点极易踩坑）；
   - 引擎每次决策都重新读 `this.config`，所以整体替换即热更新。实测替换后 45 秒回读仍是新值。
3. **枚举存活会话用 `ctx.get('agents').list()`**：
   `sessionPersistence.list()` 的条目形状是 `{ header, revision, sizeBytes }`，
   会话 id 在 `entry.header.id` 里、**顶层没有 id**；照顶层取会永远扫到 0 个会话。
4. **两条落地路径**：
   - 保存设置时立即扫描存活会话写入（实测 1.5 秒内引擎即为新值）；
   - 每个 step 边界 `ctx.on('agent/pre-step', …, { prepend: true })` 再兜底同步一次。

不改压缩算法、不碰会话日志：摘要生成、消息替换、checkpoint、持久化、溢出恢复
全部仍是官方 `compaction-basic` 负责。设置值持久化在设置存储（命名空间
`dsh-compaction-threshold`），进程重启后由 step 边界重新应用。

## 安装（本机 DSH Desktop）

Desktop 独占 profile 装配，`dsh plugin add` 在本机不可用。走本地热装配：

```
npm pack                                  # → dsh-compaction-threshold-0.1.0.tgz
# 解包到 D:\dsh-plugins\dsh-compaction-threshold
# dev_install_package(dir, profile='desktop')
```

本插件宿主半边只 import `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`（`0.2.0` 起 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-settings`
的 `installSettingsSection` / `settingsNamespace` 已删除，导入它们会让宿主起不来）。
link 安装的插件目录没有自己的 `node_modules`，因此目录内建立一个**指回内核同一份**的
junction（不是拷贝，避免版本偏移）：

```
node_modules/@deepseek-ai/schemastery → <app>/dsh/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/schemastery
```

（`<app>` = 官方 Harness 安装目录，例如 `D:\DeepSeek Harness\resources\app`。
注意**不要**指向社区 Desktop 或其它副本：目标一旦被卸载/移动，悬空链接会让插件
`failed to import`、宿主启动报错。）

装完**硬刷新页面**（Ctrl+Shift+R），在 **插件 → dsh-compaction-threshold** 的配置卡里
即可看到本行（0.2.0 起第三方插件的配置卡在插件页，不在「设置 → 通用」）。

> ⚠️ 改本插件的代码后需要**重启 DSH Desktop** 才生效：本机 super-injector 的
> `dev_reload_package` 拿不到 `loader.internal`，只会"重新装配"旧模块；
> 且 `dev_install_package` 见到已存在的 loader entry 会跳过 create。重启后由
> profile 的 bundles 列表正常装配。

## 验证

宿主日志（`%APPDATA%\DSH Desktop\logs\host\dsh-<日期>.log`）里会有：

```
[dsh-compaction-threshold] audit-><写入路径> {"event":"applied","thresholdRatio":0.62,…}
```

同时会往下列第一个可写目录追加一行 JSONL 审计（`dsh-compaction-threshold.jsonl`）：
`$DSH_HOME` → `~/.dsh` → 本插件目录。

## 限制

- 只调**阈值类**策略；压缩范围选择、摘要质量、按模型覆盖（`modelPolicies`）、
  摘要模型选择不在本插件范围内。
- 只支持**百分比**；按绝对 Token 设阈值需要知道每个模型窗口，未做。
- 若别处设过 `retainTokens`，本插件会清掉它（与 `retainRatio` 互斥）。
- 某个 preset 若没有压缩组（不压缩的 preset），`serviceFor` 拿不到引擎，本插件对它无效。

## 许可

MIT。

# 🛡️ dsh-permission-rules - **1024 store channel**: `npm i -g dsh1024` once, then `dsh1024 plugin --profile web add dsh-permission-rules` (counts toward the [deepseek1024.com](https://deepseek1024.com) install ranking). [![Gitee](https://img.shields.io/badge/Gitee-mirror-c71d23?logo=gitee)](https://gitee.com/perrylink/dsh-permission-rules) [![dshfind](https://dshfind.com/api/badge/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules?metric=downloads)](https://dshfind.com/plugins/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules?ref=badge) [![OpenSSF Scorecard](https://api.securityscorecards.dev/projects/github.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/badge)](https://api.securityscorecards.dev/projects/github.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules) **Claude Code-style declarative permission rules for DeepSeek Harness.** *Rules decide what is known. A reviewer model decides what is not.* [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![DSH plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/dsh--plugin-✅-green)](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin) [![dsh-doctor](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PerryLink/dsh-plugin-doctor/main/badges/PerryLink__dsh-permission-rules.svg)](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-plugin-doctor#verified-徽章) [![DSH Market](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/2BingLing/dsh-market/master/assets/readme/badge-top-rated.svg)](https://dsh.market/) [![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%5E22.19%20%7C%7C%20%3E%3D24-brightgreen.svg)](#) [![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/ci.yml?branch=main&label=CI)](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/actions) [![Version](https://img.shields.io/github/v/tag/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules?label=version)](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/releases) [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-permission-rules)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-permission-rules) [![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/dsh-permission-rules)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-permission-rules) [English](README.md) · [简体中文](README-zh.md) · [Español](README-es.md) · [Português](README-pt.md) · [हिन्दी](README-hi.md)
--- **📖 Ecosystem knowledge base** — measured data, not marketing: [plugin development guide · plugin-selection data · maintenance criteria](https://perrylink.github.io/dsh-plugin-guide/). ## ⭐ 如果它帮到了你 这个插件是 [DSH 插件家族](https://github.com/PerryLink)的一员（40+ 个，全部 Apache-2.0）。如果你在用，**给个 star** —— 它不会解锁任何功能，但会让下一个人在搜索里更容易找到它。 *English:* part of a 40+ plugin family for DeepSeek Harness. If it is useful, **a star helps the next person find it** — nothing is gated behind it. ## What is dsh-permission-rules? Claude Code-style declarative permission rules for DeepSeek Harness. Rules decide what is known. A reviewer model decides what is not. ![Terminal demo of dsh-permission-rules: dsh-permission-rules — deny/ask rules in one YAML file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/main/docs/assets/dsh-permission-rules-demo.png) ![Animated terminal demo of dsh-permission-rules](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/main/docs/assets/dsh-permission-rules-demo.gif) *The same run, animated.* ## Compatibility | Surface | Status | |---|---| | Harness | DeepSeek Harness `dsh-v0.2.1-alpha.1` (adapted 2026-09-22, full gate chain): its plugin config is the live settings contract — every field is declared `.volatile()`, the Loader hands `apply` a live reference per field, and a saved edit is committed into the running references WITHOUT remounting the plugin, with out-of-range values refused by the schema before anything is written. A host whose Schemastery predates `volatile()` (before 3.18.3) still mounts and runs this plugin — the fields simply stay ordinary values and the live config form is unavailable — because the marker is applied through a capability probe rather than assumed. `Session.append` on this line still cannot stamp the `ignorable` marker (its third argument is the surface-intent bag, and the envelope field survives for stored-log reads only), so the whole `0.2-alpha` line is pre-checked as unmarked and session-log audit stays disabled by default — `append` reads only `sourceEventSeqs`/`surfaceOp` and freezes the envelope, so it has no code path that could stamp the marker; the earlier `0.1.7-alpha` (adapted 2026-09-22), `0.1.5-rc.2` (adapted 2026-09-09) and `0.1.3-alpha` lines keep the same surface-only append signature, and every `0.2` prerelease is classified with them (a STABLE `0.2.x` release is left to the append probe, so a restored marker surface is adopted without a new plugin release). Those lines' log migrations refuse unclassified plugin events even when marked, so `strip` v1 audit rows before a `0.1.3-alpha` host opens the log and v2 audit rows before a `0.1.5-alpha` host migrates it (native v3 logs only need `repair`). | | Node | `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` | | Platforms | All (host + web settings client) | | Model | Any (deny/ask reasons surface through tool results) | ## What you get `dsh-permission-rules` puts an ordered **`allow` / `deny` / `ask`** rule list in front of every tool call on the `tools/pre-execute` waterfall — deterministic, instant, auditable, and written by you in plain YAML: - **`deny`** blocks the call; the rule's `reason` becomes the model-visible error. - **`ask`** rides the official approval seam (mount `dsh-auto-review` for a second-model answerer, or a human answers; with neither, the harness fails closed). - **`allow`** (and no-match) strictly delegates via `next()` — downstream listeners are never short-circuited. Every hit **and** every passthrough is audit-logged as a `permissionRules/decision` session event (log-only — nothing extra is injected into the model context). - **Rich matching** — tool-name globs (including `mcp__*`), agent-identity selectors (`main` / `subagent` / `preset:*`), argument key/value globs **or** regexes (with `!pattern` negation and an `absent` key dimension), workspace-relative path globs at **any nesting depth**, `when` host conditions (env vars, platform), and **shell command decomposition** (`argv`: command word, argument tokens, pipeline signature) for token-precise command matching. - **Built-in high-risk baseline** — a shipped deny/ask ruleset (destructive commands, privilege escalation, download-and-execute, sensitive paths) enabled by default and appended after user rules so a nearer user rule can override it; toggle with `builtin.enabled`. - **Hierarchical rule files** — optional `searchUp` merges every `.dsh/rules.yaml` from the session cwd to the filesystem root, nearest first. - **Dry-run rollout** — `enforce: false` audits what the policy *would* do while passing every call through. - **Hot reload** — Chokidar watch with debounce; a broken edit keeps the previous rules, never crashes. On a WSL host, or for a rule file under `/mnt/`, the watch switches to polling because native change events are unreliable there. - **Fail loud** — invalid YAML, unknown actions/fields, bad globs/regexes, backtracking-prone patterns, or more than `maxRules` rules fail the load. ## Rule syntax ```yaml # /.dsh/rules.yaml rules: - match: { tools: [bash, pwsh], params: { command: "git push*" }, paths: ["**/secrets/**"] } action: deny reason: "No pushes from protected paths" - match: { tools: [edit, write] } action: ask reason: "File writes need confirmation" ``` - **Match dimensions** — `tools` (globs, incl. `mcp__*`), `agents` (`main` / `subagent` / `preset:`; unknown identity never matches — fail closed), `params` (key/value globs or regexes, `!pattern` negation, `absent` key dimension), `paths` (workspace-relative globs extracted at any nesting depth), `when` (`env` var globs/regexes + a closed `platform` list), and `network` (`domains` / `ips` / `ports` / `schemes` — globs, wildcards, CIDRs, port ranges). - **Actions** — `allow` / `deny` / `ask`, evaluated in file order, first match wins. - **Rule metadata** — `enabled: false` (visible but inert), `description`, `tags`; unknown fields fail the load. - **Schema**

# dsh-intelligent-ui Interactive cards in DeepSeek Harness chats. The model writes a small interface program, the chat draws it as a native card, and every control recomputes in your browser without another model call. A button sends its text as your next message. [中文](README-zh.md) | | | |---|---| | Requires | DeepSeek Harness **>= 0.2.1-alpha.1** (below 0.3.0) | | Platforms | Web UI, macOS desktop app, and Windows desktop app — one bundle, because both desktop apps load the same web client | | Verified | Web UI 0.2.1-alpha.4; macOS and Windows desktop apps 0.2.1-rc.2 | | Install | Settings → Plugins → Add plugin → `https://github.com/StarsHarryZhu/dsh-intelligent-UI` (needs `git` on `PATH`), then restart the harness and reload the page | ## The 27 components One card per component, drawn by this plugin in the host's light theme. The program behind each card is in [`docs/SAMPLES.md`](docs/SAMPLES.md). | Component | Group | What it shows | Screenshot | |---|---|---|---| | `card` | Layout | The framed root: optional title, padding, and gap. | | | `col` | Layout | A vertical stack in reading order. | | | `row` | Layout | Equal-width cells side by side; they wrap on a narrow screen. | | | `grid` | Layout | An even grid of one to four columns. | | | `title` | Text | A headline line in five sizes. | | | `text` | Text | A sentence, with `{…}` live values. | | | `badge` | Text | A one-word status label in five tones. | | | `callout` | Text | One emphasized remark: an assumption, a caveat, a next step. | | | `divider` | Text | A hairline separator. | | | `link` | Text | A citation link, opened only when clicked. | | | `image` | Text | An inline `data:` image with alt text and a caption. | | | `metric` | Data | One prominent number that recomputes as controls move. | | | `progress` | Data | A proportion bar. | | | `table` | Data | A comparison table; `current=` highlights a row. | | | `keys` | Data | Label and value pairs for exact figures. | | | `list` | Data | A bulleted list; `current=` highlights an item. | | | `steps` | Data | A numbered procedure; with `mono=true` and `current=`, a code listing with the running line highlighted. | | | `chart` | Data | A bar or line chart. | | | `plot` | Math | Curves of y = f(x) with a marked point, its tangent, and a shaded integral. | | | `formula` | Math | A typeset expression with its live value. | | | `slider` | Controls | A range slider bound to a number. | | | `numberInput` | Controls | Exact number entry. | | | `textInput` | Controls | A one-line text field. | | | `select` | Controls | A dropdown choice. | | | `checkbox` | Controls | An on/off switch. | | | `button` | Action | Sends its text as your next message, then locks the card. | | | `player` | Animation | A control bar at the bottom of the card: plays, pauses, steps, and scrubs a number at 0.5× to 2×; everything that reads it follows. | | ## How it works - The plugin registers one tool, `ui_render`, and one skill, `dsh-intelligent-ui`, which teaches the model when a card beats prose. The model never writes HTML or JavaScript: its program is checked against the 27-component catalog and stored with the tool result. - A card draws in the tool row while the reply streams, and under the reply once it finishes. Moving a control recomputes every figure locally. - A `player` animates a card: code traced line by line, an algorithm's passes, a point moving along a curve. Playback runs in the browser and sends nothing to the model. - Cards compute integrals (including infinite bounds), derivatives, limits, sums and products, roots, and Taylor polynomials. A value that cannot be computed reliably shows "—", never a guess. - Uninstalling leaves every session opening as before; earlier calls show as ordinary tool rows. ## Development ```sh node scripts/link-dev.mjs # link the toolchain from the sibling harness checkout node build.js # type-check, build, and self-check the bundle node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run ``` `AGENTS.md` holds the rules of the tree; `docs/VERIFY.md` is the live checklist. ## License [MIT License](LICENSE) © 2026 Starfield.

plugins.description: WorkBuddy credit sidebar panel for DeepSeek Harness: Deepseek Harness插件，查看积分详情最高效、最直观的方式
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-workbuddy-credits

[DeepSeek Harness](https://www.deepseek.com/harness/) 的 Web 侧栏面板：随时查看 **WorkBuddy / CodeBuddy 账号积分**——余额、到期分布、免费模型与倍率，带手动刷新。

> A resident Web sidebar panel for DeepSeek Harness that shows your WorkBuddy account credits: balance, expiry spread, free models, and per-model rates, with manual refresh.

```
┌─ WorkBuddy 积分 ───────────────────────── 更新于 18:42:07 ── [刷新] ┐
│  国内版 │ 国际版                                                    │
│                                                                     │
│  ┌─合计余额───┐ ┌─7 天内过期─┐ ┌─免费模型─┐ ┌─套餐数─┐           │
│  │ 5,006 积分 │ │   40 积分  │ │    2     │ │   15   │           │
│  └────────────┘ └────────────┘ └──────────┘ └────────┘           │
│                                                                     │
│  ⚠ 7 天内有 40 积分过期（1 个包），最早 2026-10-19 12:13            │
│                                                                     │
│  到期时间            剩余      总量     剩余时长   套餐             │
│  2026-10-19 12:13       40      100     0.5 天   …运营裂变包        │
│  2026-10-26 09:33    2,000    2,000     7.4 天   Buddy AI个人标准版 │
│  2026-10-26 09:33    2,000    2,000     7.4 天   Codebuddy版本赠送包│
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## 为什么需要它

积分读取**每次都会真实调用上游计费接口**（实测 200–500 ms）。直接查既慢又费额度，而定时轮询会持续消耗你想监控的那个额度。
自带的积分监控有时会无法显示消失掉，在界面位置过小，且不能显示套餐过期详情。

这个面板把读取放进**宿主侧缓存**：开关面板、切换会话、重开页面都只读内存，只有按下「刷新」才真正打上游。

| | 实测 |
|---|---|
| 冷读（真实上游） | ~210–370 ms |
| 热读（缓存） | **2–3 ms** |
| 自动轮询 | **没有** |

## 安装

```bash
dsh plugin add dsh-workbuddy-credits
```

**前置条件**：需要先装好并登录 [`dsh-workbuddy-connect`](https://github.com/corrinehu/dsh-workbuddy-connect)——积分属于 WorkBuddy 桌面端账号，本插件复用它的登录态，自己不做认证。

安装后侧栏会出现「WorkBuddy 积分」图标。国内版（`workbuddy.cn`）与国际版（WorkBuddy AI）的账号与积分互不相通，用面板顶部的分段按钮切换。

## 设计要点

- **不自己读账号。** 只读 `dsh-workbuddy-connect` 的状态路由并加缓存；认证与计费协议都由上游插件负责，它升级时本插件不必跟着改。
- **stale-while-revalidate。** 缓存过期时立刻返回旧数据、后台再刷新，永远不让人等计费接口。
- **失败保留数据。** 刷新失败时保留上一次成功的数字，并标注「刷新失败」及原因，而不是把面板变成一片空白。未登录 / 令牌过期是**数据状态**而不是报错。
- **不缓存未登录。** 只有可用的积分数据才进缓存，否则登录后会被缓存挡住一整个周期。
- **并发合并。** 同一时刻的多个刷新请求合并成一次上游调用。
- **只读 + loopback 防护。** 路由只接受 `GET`，且要求 `Host` 与 `Origin` 都是回环地址（防 DNS rebinding）。它不写任何账号状态。
- **无构建步骤。** `client.js` 是手写的浏览器模块工厂，仓库里就是运行时真正加载的代码。

### 缓存与数据流

```
面板 (client.js)
   │  fetch /plugins/dsh-workbuddy-credits/status?provider=…&refresh=0|1
   ▼
本插件宿主半侧 (index.js)   ←── 60s 缓存，并发合并，投影 + 排序
   │  GET /plugins/dsh-workbuddy-connect/status
   ▼
dsh-workbuddy-connect        ←── 复用桌面端登录态
   │  HTTPS
   ▼
WorkBuddy 上游计费接口        ←── 真实计费查询
```

## 配置

缓存时长在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里调整：

```yaml
- id: workbuddy-credits
  name: dsh-workbuddy-credits
  config:
    cacheTtlMs: 60000   # 默认 60 秒，上限 3600000（1 小时）
```

调大更省额度、数据更旧；调小更实时。无论多大，手动刷新都会绕开它。

## HTTP 接口

面板走的那条路由也可以直接调用，适合脚本化：

```bash
# 缓存读取
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:19387/plugins/dsh-workbuddy-credits/status'

# 强制真实读取上游
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:19387/plugins/dsh-workbuddy-credits/status?refresh=1'

# 国际版
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:19387/plugins/dsh-workbuddy-credits/status?provider=workbuddy-ai'
```

响应字段：

| 字段 | 含义 |
|---|---|
| `state` | `ready` / `signed-out` / `unavailable` |
| `total` | 合计余额 |
| `accounts[]` | 积分包，**按到期时间升序**；`endTimeMs: null` 表示无到期时间 |
| `expiry.within{24h,3d,7d}` | 各窗口内即将过期的合计与包数 |
| `models[]` | 模型，**按倍率升序**（越低越省） |
| `freeModels[]` | 免费模型 |
| `cached` / `stale` / `ageMs` | 是否来自缓存、是否为过期数据、缓存年龄 |
| `refreshError` | 刷新失败时的原因（此时数据仍是上次成功的） |

上游返回 `signed-in` 以外、或无法识别的状态时，一律按 `unavailable` 处理，不会误报成「未登录」把你引去重新登录。


## 已知限制

- **只读。** 不做充值、扣减或任何账号写操作。
- **依赖 `dsh-workbuddy-connect`。** 没装或没登录时，面板会明确显示「未登录」并给出提示。
- **数值仅供参考。** 倍率与实际价格的关系由上游决定，折算只能给量级估算。
- **企业账号**走周期重置额度，没有普通包的到期语义。
- **缓存是进程内的。** 重启 DSH 后第一次打开面板会真实读一次上游。

## 作者

Fancy Lee（[@fancylear](https://github.com/fancylear)）

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

plugins.readme_text:
# @deepwhale-cn/dsh-secret-scan

[![Listed on DSH Plugin Hub](https://dsh-plugin.org/badges/listed.svg)](https://dsh-plugin.org/zh/plugins/feely0208/dsh-secret-scan)

**密钥与敏感信息扫描** —— 给 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 用的 skill 插件。

提交前、发布前、开源前，把不该出现在代码里的东西找出来。

这是这一组技能里唯一**通用**的（不限中国大陆）—— 因为"密钥进了仓库"是所有技术团队都会踩的坑。

## 它能扫出什么（7 条规则）

技能负责「怎么处理」，规则引擎负责「有没有」。一条命令出证据：

```bash
dsh-secret-scan --root <项目路径>   # 扫一遍
dsh-secret-scan --demo             # 看内置演示样本
dsh-secret-scan --list-rules       # 列出规则与依据
```

| 规则 | 查什么 | 级别 |
|---|---|---|
| `SECRET-PRIVATE-KEY` | PEM 私钥块（标签 + 后面真跟着密钥正文）| 严重 |
| `SECRET-AWS-AKID` | `AKIA` + 16 位 | 高 |
| `SECRET-GITHUB-TOKEN` | `gh[pousr]_` / `github_pat_` | 高 |
| `SECRET-SLACK-TOKEN` | `xox[baprs]-` / `xapp-` | 高 |
| `SECRET-STRIPE-LIVE` | `sk_live_` / `rk_live_` | 高 |
| `SECRET-CREDENTIAL-LITERAL` | 变量名含 secret/token/password + 高熵字面量 | 中 |
| `SECRET-STRIPE-PUBLISHABLE` | `pk_live_` —— **Stripe 官方说可公开，故单列低级别** | 低 |

**输出不落原值**：正则只消费前缀或变量名，密钥正文放在零宽断言里，
所以报告里的证据是 `AKIA` / `ghp_` / `secretAccessKey` 这种，**不含密钥本身**。

**只写标签不写正文不报**（文档里贴格式示意不误报）；`process.env.SECRET` 这类不报。

**已知边界**：`.pem` / `.key` / `.p12` 文件本体不被引擎当文本读（core 的扩展名名单没收录），
直接放 `server.pem` 会漏；同样私钥写成 `id_rsa` 或贴进代码/文档则能命中。报告会如实列出「跳过文件」。

## 它查什么

| 类别 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| 🔴 **高置信令牌** | 云厂商 Access Key（AKIA/LTAI/AKID）、GitHub/npm/Slack 令牌、Google API Key |
| 🔴 **私钥与证书** | `id_rsa`、`*.pem`/`*.p12`/`*.jks`，以及嵌在代码里的 PEM 私钥内容 |
| 🔴 **凭据文件进了 git** | `.env`、`credentials.json`、`.npmrc` 等是否已被 `git ls-files` 跟踪 |
| 🟠 **配置里的敏感赋值** | `password=` / `token=` / `api_key=` 这类硬编码（误报较多，逐条看） |
| 🟠 **内部信息** | 内网 IP（`10.` / `192.168.` / `172.16-31.`）、内部域名（`.corp` / `.internal`） |

**退出码 1 = 有高置信命中**，可直接挂到 pre-commit 或 CI 上。

## 两条刻意的设计

**1. 输出默认打码**（只留前后 4 位）。

扫描工具把完整密钥打进终端或日志，等于换个地方又泄露一次。要看全必须显式 `--reveal`，
而且别把输出存进文件或贴进聊天。

**2. 技能正文里，处置顺序比扫描本身更重要**：

```
1. 轮换密钥  →  2. 清理代码  →  3. 再决定要不要改写历史
```

**删代码不会让已泄露的密钥失效** —— 它还在 git 历史、已推送的远端副本、CI 日志与缓存、
你的 shell 历史和编辑器备份里。判断标准很简单：**这个密钥有没有离开过你的机器？**

一个只教人"删掉就好"的工具，是在帮倒忙。

## 误报怎么办

文档里的示例值（`your-api-key-here`、`sk-example-...`）**已自动过滤**。测试用的假密钥建议
写成含 `example` / `dummy` 的明显假值，同样会被过滤。

剩下的 🟠 逐条看上下文 —— 但**别因为误报多就不看报告了**，那正是这类工具失效的方式。

## 安装

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @deepwhale-cn/dsh-secret-scan
```

## 用法

```bash
# 脚本路径由插件注册时注入到技能正文里，或到安装目录找 skill/scan.sh
scan.sh --dir /path/to/repo          # 默认打码
scan.sh --dir /path/to/repo --reveal # ⚠️ 打印完整密钥，仅排障时用
```

## 与相邻技能的边界

| 包 | 管什么 |
| --- | --- |
| **`dsh-secret-scan`** | **内部信息进了代码仓库**（该不该提交、提交了怎么补救） |
| `dsh-cn-compliance` 的 I 类 | **内部文件的公网暴露面**（被搜索引擎或公开链接读到） |

两者的交集是"内部信息"，但一个看**版本控制**，一个看**暴露面**。

## 许可

MIT

---

## 深鲸网安守护系列（共 31 个）

> 一个插件做一件事。**安全问题是链式的** —— 配套用才完整。

**国内合规** ｜ [等保对照](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-mlps) · [日志留存](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-log-retention) · [备案公示](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-filing) · [用户同意](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-consent-guard) · [个人信息权利](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-data-rights) · [未成年人保护](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-minor-guard) · [影响评估](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-pipia) · [数据分类分级](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-data-classify) · [算法备案](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-algorithm-filing) · [数据出境](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-data-export) · [国密合规](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-crypto) · [AI 内容标识](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-ai-labeling)

**AI 与 Agent 治理** ｜ [AI 输出信任](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-ai-output-trust) · [外部内容信任](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-content-trust) · [MCP 安全](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-mcp-audit) · [Agent 权限](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-agent-scope) · [策略核对](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-agent-policy) · [可疑指令](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-phishing-guard)

**数据与凭据** ｜ [敏感数据](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-data-scan) · [密钥轮换](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-key-rotate) · [数据留存](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-data-lifecycle) · [配置审计](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-env-audit) · [**密钥扫描**](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-secret-scan)

**供应链与构建** ｜ [开源许可](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-license-guard) · [依赖投毒](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-dep-audit) · [CI 安全](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-ci-guard) · [工具审查](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-tool-vet) · [物料清单](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-sbom)

Rules decide what is known. A reviewer model decides what is not. ![Terminal demo of dsh-permission-rules: dsh-permission-rules — deny/ask rules in one YAML file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/main/docs/assets/dsh-permission-rules-demo.png) ![Animated terminal demo of dsh-permission-rules](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/main/docs/assets/dsh-permission-rules-demo.gif) *The same run, animated.* ## Compatibility | Surface | Status | |---|---| | Harness | DeepSeek Harness `dsh-v0.2.1-alpha.1` (adapted 2026-09-22, full gate chain): its plugin config is the live settings contract — every field is declared `.volatile()`, the Loader hands `apply` a live reference per field, and a saved edit is committed into the running references WITHOUT remounting the plugin, with out-of-range values refused by the schema before anything is written. A host whose Schemastery predates `volatile()` (before 3.18.3) still mounts and runs this plugin — the fields simply stay ordinary values and the live config form is unavailable — because the marker is applied through a capability probe rather than assumed. `Session.append` on this line still cannot stamp the `ignorable` marker (its third argument is the surface-intent bag, and the envelope field survives for stored-log reads only), so the whole `0.2-alpha` line is pre-checked as unmarked and session-log audit stays disabled by default — `append` reads only `sourceEventSeqs`/`surfaceOp` and freezes the envelope, so it has no code path that could stamp the marker; the earlier `0.1.7-alpha` (adapted 2026-09-22), `0.1.5-rc.2` (adapted 2026-09-09) and `0.1.3-alpha` lines keep the same surface-only append signature, and every `0.2` prerelease is classified with them (a STABLE `0.2.x` release is left to the append probe, so a restored marker surface is adopted without a new plugin release). Those lines' log migrations refuse unclassified plugin events even when marked, so `strip` v1 audit rows before a `0.1.3-alpha` host opens the log and v2 audit rows before a `0.1.5-alpha` host migrates it (native v3 logs only need `repair`). | | Node | `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` | | Platforms | All (host + web settings client) | | Model | Any (deny/ask reasons surface through tool results) | ## What you get `dsh-permission-rules` puts an ordered **`allow` / `deny` / `ask`** rule list in front of every tool call on the `tools/pre-execute` waterfall — deterministic, instant, auditable, and written by you in plain YAML: - **`deny`** blocks the call; the rule's `reason` becomes the model-visible error. - **`ask`** rides the official approval seam (mount `dsh-auto-review` for a second-model answerer, or a human answers; with neither, the harness fails closed). - **`allow`** (and no-match) strictly delegates via `next()` — downstream listeners are never short-circuited. Every hit **and** every passthrough is audit-logged as a `permissionRules/decision` session event (log-only — nothing extra is injected into the model context). - **Rich matching** — tool-name globs (including `mcp__*`), agent-identity selectors (`main` / `subagent` / `preset:*`), argument key/value globs **or** regexes (with `!pattern` negation and an `absent` key dimension), workspace-relative path globs at **any nesting depth**, `when` host conditions (env vars, platform), and **shell command decomposition** (`argv`: command word, argument tokens, pipeline signature) for token-precise command matching. - **Built-in high-risk baseline** — a shipped deny/ask ruleset (destructive commands, privilege escalation, download-and-execute, sensitive paths) enabled by default and appended after user rules so a nearer user rule can override it; toggle with `builtin.enabled`. - **Hierarchical rule files** — optional `searchUp` merges every `.dsh/rules.yaml` from the session cwd to the filesystem root, nearest first. - **Dry-run rollout** — `enforce: false` audits what the policy *would* do while passing every call through. - **Hot reload** — Chokidar watch with debounce; a broken edit keeps the previous rules, never crashes. On a WSL host, or for a rule file under `/mnt/`, the watch switches to polling because native change events are unreliable there. - **Fail loud** — invalid YAML, unknown actions/fields, bad globs/regexes, backtracking-prone patterns, or more than `maxRules` rules fail the load. ## Rule syntax ```yaml # /.dsh/rules.yaml rules: - match: { tools: [bash, pwsh], params: { command: "git push*" }, paths: ["**/secrets/**"] } action: deny reason: "No pushes from protected paths" - match: { tools: [edit, write] } action: ask reason: "File writes need confirmation" ``` - **Match dimensions** — `tools` (globs, incl. `mcp__*`), `agents` (`main` / `subagent` / `preset:`; unknown identity never matches — fail closed), `params` (key/value globs or regexes, `!pattern` negation, `absent` key dimension), `paths` (workspace-relative globs extracted at any nesting depth), `when` (`env` var globs/regexes + a closed `platform` list), and `network` (`domains` / `ips` / `ports` / `schemes` — globs, wildcards, CIDRs, port ranges). - **Actions** — `allow` / `deny` / `ask`, evaluated in file order, first match wins. - **Rule metadata** — `enabled: false` (visible but inert), `description`, `tags`; unknown fields fail the load. - **Schema**

plugins.description: Command resolution forensics: which file a command actually runs, what it shadows, and whether the copies agree.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-which

**Command resolution forensics for DeepSeek Harness.** When you type `node`, a shell answers with a rule that is longer than people remember — PATH order, then PATHEXT on Windows or the executable bit elsewhere, with builtins short-circuiting the whole thing. `dsh-which` reports what that rule actually decided, what it shadowed, what shape PATH itself is in, and whether the copies behind one name agree on a version.

Every failure it names is silent. The command runs; it is just not the one you meant.

```
dsh-which · node
  winner:   C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.EXE
  kind:     native binary
  from:     PATH[0]  C:\Program Files\nodejs
  size:     84MB
  modified: 2025-11-03T09:14:00.000Z
  version:  v24.13.0  (--version)
  searched: 9 PATH entries

  shadowed — 1 other directory holds this name:
    PATH[6]  C:\Users\me\scoop\shims\node.EXE  native binary  84MB
      ↳ reports v20.11.1

  ⚠ the copies behind this name report different versions — the one that runs is the one at PATH[0].
```

That last block is the whole reason this exists. Two Node installations, one on PATH, and nothing anywhere tells you which one a command gets.

## Why not just run `which`

1. **`which` does not exist on Windows**, and where it does exist it answers a narrower question. It reports the file it found; it does not report the file it skipped.
2. **`which` inherits the rules under investigation.** Shelling out to a resolver to explain resolution means trusting the resolver you are debugging. The rules here are reimplemented as pure functions over an injected filesystem (`lib/resolve.js`), so they are testable against fixtures instead of against whatever is installed on the test machine.
3. **Shell builtins are not files.** `which cd` on most systems walks every PATH entry to report something that has nothing to do with what runs. This plugin says `builtin` and explains that PATH was never consulted.
4. **The interesting output is the shadowed copy.** "What runs" is one line. "What else answers to this name, and why is it not running" is the diagnosis — a stale global install behind a fresh local one, a `.cmd` shim in front of a real binary, a file that exists but was never made executable.
5. **Reporting is the whole job.** There is no PATH-editing tool here. A plugin that silently rewrites PATH is a plugin that breaks a machine.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin add https://github.com/11111353535/dsh-which
```

From a checkout instead of a git host, pass the absolute path:

```sh
dsh plugin add /absolute/path/to/dsh-which
```

Optional configuration, in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: which
  name: 'dsh-which'
  config:
    probeByDefault: false        # run a version probe on every resolve
    probeShadowedByDefault: false # probe the shadowed copies too
    probeTimeoutMs: 4000
    maxSweepFiles: 400
    runtimes: [node, npm, pnpm, python, git]
```

| key | default | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `probeTimeoutMs` | `4000` | How long a version probe may take before it is abandoned. |
| `probeByDefault` | `false` | Probe every resolve without being asked. Slower, explains more. |
| `probeShadowedByDefault` | `false` | Probe the shadowed copies too. Multiplies the process spawns. |
| `maxSweepFiles` | `400` | Files examined in one sweep, so a huge directory cannot stall a session. |
| `runtimes` | node, npm, pnpm, yarn, bun, python, python3, pip, pip3, uv, git, rg, fd, make, pwsh, bash | Commands the environment report resolves. |

Probing is off by default because it spawns processes, and a diagnostic that costs four seconds on every call is a diagnostic people turn off.

## Tools

### `which_resolve`

Resolve one command and report what runs, what it shadowed, and — on request — what each copy reports as its version.

| parameter | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `command` | string, **required** | A name (`node`) or a path (`./build.sh`, `C:\tools\x.exe`). |
| `probe` | boolean | Run the winner with a version flag. |
| `probeShadowed` | boolean | Probe the shadowed copies too, so versions can be compared. |

A name that resolves to nothing is an answer, not an error:

```
dsh-which · build
  not found
  the name exists on PATH but nothing with that name is runnable
  searched: 45 PATH entries

  the name exists, but nothing with it can run:
        build  not runnable  1KB
        build  not runnable  1KB
        build  not runnable  1KB
        build  not runnable  1KB
        build  not runnable  1KB
        build  not runnable  1KB
        build  not runnable  1KB
        build  not runnable  1KB
        … and 37 more
```

The count is the finding; the enumeration is the evidence, and past eight directories the evidence stops being read. The lines that save an hour are the second and third: the name *is* on PATH, the file simply cannot run. On POSIX that means no executable bit — a shell walks right past it into later PATH entries, or fails.

An explicit path never consults PATH, and the report says so:

```
dsh-which · /repo/scripts/build.sh
  winner:   /repo/scripts/build.sh
  kind:     script
  from:     given as a path, PATH was not consulted
  size:     2.3KB
  searched: 0 PATH entries
```

### `which_path`

The shape of PATH itself: every entry in resolution order, with duplicates, entries whose directory is gone, and entries containing an unexpanded variable.

| parameter | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `showNoise` | boolean | Include `/usr/bin`, `/bin` and friends, omitted by default as uninformative. |
| `limit` | number | Maximum entries listed. Defaults to 40. |

```
dsh-which · PATH
  9 entries · 8 unique directories
  1 duplicate entry · 1 dead entry

  entries, in resolution order:
    [ 0] C:\Program Files\nodejs
    [ 1] C:\Users\me\AppData\Roaming\npm
    [ 2] C:\Windows\system32
    [ 3] C:\Windows
    [ 4] C:\tools\git\cmd
    [ 5] C:\Program Files\nodejs  — dup of [0]
    [ 6] C:\Users\me\scoop\shims
    [ 7] D:\old-python\Scripts  — missing
    [ 8] C:\Users\me\bin

  Duplicates are usually an installer that prepends itself on every run. Harmless until you edit "the" entry and two copies of it remain.

  Dead entries are skipped silently by every shell, so an uninstalled toolchain leaves a hole that only shows up when its command fails.
```

A dead entry is invisible by construction: shells skip it without a word, so the hole only surfaces later as "command not found" for something that was there yesterday. An unexpanded `%USERPROFILE%` is worse — it can never resolve, no matter what the variable is set to.

### `which_env`

One page describing the command environment: platform, shell, working directory, PATH findings, PATHEXT, and where each common runtime resolves from.

| parameter | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | number | Maximum runtimes listed. Defaults to 30. |

```
dsh-which · environment
  platform: win32  arch x64  node v24.13.0
  shell:    pwsh.exe  (C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe)
  cwd:      C:\repo
  PATH:     9 entries · 8 unique
            1 duplicate · 1 dead
  PATHEXT:  .COM .EXE .BAT .CMD

  resolved runtimes:
    · node  C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.EXE
    · npm  C:\Program Files\nodejs\npm.CMD
    · pnpm  C:\Users\me\AppData\Roaming\npm\pnpm.CMD
    · git  C:\tools\git\cmd\git.EXE
    ✗ python  not found

  1 runtime(s) exist in more than one place on PATH: node
```

The shell line matters more than it looks. `pwsh` and `cmd` disagree about builtins and about `.ps1`, so a report that names the wrong shell is a report nobody should trust.

### `which_sweep`

Sweep a directory of scripts and report, for each name that looks like a command, whether the copy in *that* directory is the one that would run.

| parameter | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `directory` | string, **required** | Absolute, or relative to the workspace. |
| `limit` | number | Maximum rows listed. Defaults to 60. |

```
dsh-which · sweep C:\repo\scripts
  3 command(s)
  1 resolve outside this directory (shown with ↪)
  1 do not resolve at all
